record.paper_title: Chapter 15: Open Questions and Future Directions in Titan Science
record.context_brief: Composition of Titan lakes and seas
record.original_question: What are the compositions of Titan's hydrocarbon seas and lakes, including the relative abundances of methane, ethane, and minor dissolved organic constituents such as hydrogen cyanide and acrylonitrile, and what remote-sensing or in situ measurements are needed to determine those fractions?

evidence.quote: 9) What is the composition of Titan seas and lakes?

In addition, Ontario’s composition appears to be substantially different from the large northern seas, being apparently composed mostly of ethane (Brown et al., 2008), significantly less volatile than the methane-rich northern seas (Mastrogiuseppe et al., 2019).

However, to truly determine the fractions of minor constituents dissolved in the lakes will ultimately require direct measurements through a probe sent to sample the lakes (e.g. Stofan et al., 2013; Rodriguez et al., 2022).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Titan, the largest moon of Saturn, hosts stable surface bodies of liquid hydrocarbons at cryogenic temperatures (~90–94 K), including large northern seas (Kraken Mare, Ligeia Mare, Punga Mare) and the smaller southern lake Ontario Lacus. These liquids are believed to be mixtures of methane (CH4) and ethane (C2H6) with smaller amounts of dissolved nitrogen and trace organic species such as hydrogen cyanide (HCN) and acrylonitrile (C2H3CN), among others. Existing radar and spectroscopic observations from the Cassini mission suggest that the northern seas are methane-rich and relatively volatile, while Ontario Lacus appears to be dominated by ethane, but the quantitative composition of each lake or sea, and in particular the mole fractions of minor dissolved organic constituents, remain undetermined.

Problem. (a) Determine, for each of Titan's major seas (Kraken Mare, Ligeia Mare, Punga Mare) and for Ontario Lacus, the mole-fraction composition of the liquid: specifically the relative abundances of methane and ethane, the dissolved nitrogen content, and the concentrations of minor dissolved organic constituents including hydrogen cyanide and acrylonitrile. (b) Identify and specify the remote-sensing techniques (e.g., radar bathymetry and loss-tangent measurements, near-infrared and microwave spectroscopy, thermal emission) and/or in situ measurement strategies (e.g., a lake-sampling probe with mass spectrometry) that would, in principle, suffice to determine these compositional fractions to a stated quantitative accuracy, and analyze what each technique can and cannot constrain.
artifact.status_search_result: The compositional makeup of Titan's seas and lakes, particularly the abundances of minor dissolved species like HCN and acrylonitrile, remains an open question in planetary science. Cassini-derived constraints (e.g., Mastrogiuseppe et al. on Ligeia Mare methane content; Brown et al. on Ontario Lacus ethane signatures) provide partial answers for major components, but precise minor-constituent fractions await future missions; proposed concepts such as Titan lake probes (e.g., TiME, POSEIDON) have not yet flown, and Dragonfly (planned arrival ~2034) targets dunes rather than the lakes.

status_evidence.title: Cassini radar measurement of the composition of Ligeia Mare
status_evidence.snippet: Mastrogiuseppe et al. (2019) infer Ligeia Mare is methane-rich based on radar loss-tangent analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Major-component composition of the northern seas is partially constrained but minor species are not.

status_evidence.title: The identification of liquid ethane in Titan's Ontario Lacus
status_evidence.snippet: Brown et al. (2008) reported near-infrared spectroscopic detection of ethane in Ontario Lacus.
status_evidence.claim: Ontario Lacus appears ethane-dominated, distinct from the northern seas.

status_evidence.title: POSEIDON / Titan lake probe mission concepts
status_evidence.snippet: Rodriguez et al. (2022) describe in situ probe concepts needed to determine minor dissolved constituents.
status_evidence.claim: Direct measurement of minor constituents requires a future in situ probe; problem remains open.
